doctor.specialty: Consultant Cardiologist with subspecialty expertise in interventional cardiology
bio: Dr Maggie He is a Consultant Cardiologist with subspecialty expertise in interventional cardiology. She is known for her calm, patient-centred approach and her ability to clearly explain heart conditions and treatment options, helping patients feel informed, supported, and confident in their care.

She has a strong interest in the management of coronary artery disease and heart attack care, combining advanced procedural skills with evidence-based, individualised treatment. She takes a holistic approach to cardiovascular health, recognising the importance of prevention, lifestyle, medical therapy, and long-term risk reduction alongside procedural care.

Dr He completed two years of dedicated interventional cardiology fellowship training, first at Gold Coast University Hospital and then through the prestigious Australia and New Zealand Endovascular Therapies (ANZET) Fellowship at Leeds General Infirmary in the United Kingdom — the busiest primary PCI (heart attack) centre in the UK. Through this fellowship she gained extensive experience in high-volume, complex, and high-risk coronary angioplasty and stenting, including the treatment of left main disease, heavily calcified arteries, and acute heart attacks.

Prior to her subspecialty training, Dr He completed her cardiology advanced training at Gold Coast University Hospital and Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane, achieving Fellowship of the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (FRACP). Alongside her clinical work, she remains active in medical education and research, holding a Senior Lecturer position at Griffith University's School of Medicine and Dentistry and contributing to international peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations.

investigations.name: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.description: A quick, painless recording of your heart's electrical activity.

investigations.name: Echocardiogram
investigations.description: An ultrasound scan of your heart to assess how it is pumping and check the valves.

investigations.name: Exercise stress test / stress echocardiography
investigations.description: Monitoring your heart while you walk on a treadmill, or with dobutamine, to check for reduced blood flow.

investigations.name: Holter monitor
investigations.description: A portable heart monitor worn for a period of days to detect rhythm problems.

investigations.name: 24-hour blood pressure monitor
investigations.description: A cuff worn for 24 hours to get an accurate picture of your blood pressure.

investigations.name: CT calcium score / CT coronary angiography (CTCA)
investigations.description: Non-invasive imaging to assess for coronary artery disease.

procedures.name: Coronary angiography
procedures.description: A catheter-based test to look directly at the arteries supplying your heart.

procedures.name: Coronary angioplasty and stenting (PCI)
procedures.description: Opening a narrowed or blocked heart artery and placing a stent to keep it open, including complex and high-risk cases.

procedures.name: Intravascular imaging-guided angioplasty
procedures.description: Detailed imaging from inside the artery (IVUS/OCT) to guide precise stent placement.

procedures.name: Coronary physiology and pressure wire assessment
procedures.description: Measuring blood flow and pressure across a narrowing to determine whether it needs treatment.

procedures.name: Calcium modification techniques
procedures.description: Rotational atherectomy, orbital atherectomy, and intravascular lithotripsy to treat heavily calcified coronary arteries.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral?
faqs.answer: Yes. To claim a Medicare rebate for your consultation, you will need a valid referral from your GP or another specialist. Please bring your referral letter to your first appointment.

faqs.question: What happens at the first appointment?
faqs.answer: Your first consultation typically lasts 30 to 45 minutes. Dr He will take a detailed history, perform a clinical examination, review any previous tests, and discuss a plan with you. If further tests are needed, she will explain what they involve and why.

faqs.question: Will I get a Medicare rebate?
faqs.answer: Most consultations attract a Medicare rebate when you have a valid referral. Private health insurance may cover hospital-based costs for procedures, depending on your level of cover. Please check your policy or ask the rooms for guidance.

faqs.question: Can I be seen urgently?
faqs.answer: If you have new or worsening chest pain, severe breathlessness, or feel like your heart is racing and you feel unwell, please call 000 or go to your nearest Emergency Department. For urgent but non-emergency concerns, please call the rooms and we will do our best to see you promptly.

faqs.question: What should I bring to my appointment?
faqs.answer: Please bring your referral letter, a list of your current medications, any recent test results or letters from other doctors, and your Medicare and private health insurance details if applicable. If you have specific questions, it helps to write them down beforehand.
